newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman disappointed at Defiance decision.
newsitem.headline: Goodman disappointed at Defiance decision.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Monday it was disappointed by the decision of the New Zealand Commerce Commission not to clear its planned purchase of the NZ milling and baking assets of Defiance Mills Ltd.
"We are clearly disappointed and will review the decision and respond in the near future," a spokesman for chief executive David Hearn told Reuters.

NZ Commerce Commission chairman Alan Bollard said the commission was not satisfied that, should the acquisition go ahead, Goodman Fielder would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in a number of markets.
Goodman announced the proposed NZ$48 million purchase in March when it released its half year results, saying it would allow the company to consolidate its market position in New Zealand.
The purchase was expected to be finalised by the end of April, it said.
Goodman chairman David Clarke told a media briefing at the time that the company's advice was that Commerce Commission approval would be forthcoming.
Defiance is the subject of an opposed A$97 million takeover bid by the Latin America-based Bunge Group.
The conditional sale of its New Zealand milling and baking assets was announced after Bunge launched its A$1.70 per share offer.
